agent.problem: This stop relies too heavily on discovery questions. Cards 2, 4, 6, 16 and 18 ask for facts that cannot be inferred from the earlier cards: whether to enter Samaritan towns, whether to raise the dead, how the twelve received, how to respond to rejection and which two cities Jesus names. A baker who does not already know the passage must guess rather than reason through most of the stop's choices.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The earlier cards never say how the twelve received, so the baker cannot infer “freely” from “give the same way they received.” This blank asks for unseen wording rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: After card 16 has asked about the dust gesture, this card merely repeats “Shake off the dust” and adds a joke about the junk drawer. It introduces no new passage beat and does not carry the walkthrough into verse 15, making it a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

agent.problem: The setup mentions being handed over to councils, but nothing in the earlier cards points to synagogues rather than markets or courtyards as the place of flogging. The baker can only guess this unseen location detail.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The preceding promise that the twelve will be given what to say does not identify who will speak through them. Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out “Spirit” rather than “Angel” or “Prophet,” so this becomes a guess at the verse's next word.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

human.problem: The last card is only the line saying the teaching isn't over. It tells no verse, but it cites Matthew 10:25.
human.question: What should a story card cite when it carries only the story-isn't-over line and tells no verses? Should it repeat the last verse, cite the stop's range, or cite nothing?
